audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Yasuo levels 2, 3 and first item while every matching why describes Sylas winning them, on a 54.96% win rate over 917 games. Packet chart reads Sylas for rows 0-5 and Yasuo only at two items.
audit.why: Sylas has the stronger early kit into a champion with no sustain and a 25-second Wind Wall that cannot cover every commit. Yasuo only takes over once crit items let his rotation outrun the W heal.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 flipped to Sylas in both layers with ratings rescaled; row 6 left with Yasuo.

audit.why: Four spikes at level 2, level 6, first item and late. Correct timings; the level 6 entry's content was wrong (see point 4) but the spike itself is real.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text rewritten to state Last Breath's actual casting condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) The page says Sylas 'hook-stuns' Yasuo, tells you to 'land W while he is stunned', and calls E2 an 'E2 stun' — Sylas's E recast only pulls him to the target; there is no CC in the ability at all. (b) Wind Wall's cooldown is given as 'roughly 26 seconds'; it is 25/23/21/19/17. (c) Most importantly, the page tells you to steal Last Breath and 'use it to initiate' — Last Breath blinks to an Airborne enemy champion, and Sylas's kit contains no knockup, so a stolen Last Breath is uncastable unless someone else provides the airborne first.
audit.why: The Last Breath error is the one that loses games: a player counts the Hijack as an engage tool, presses R at level 6 with nothing in the air, and finds the ability will not cast. The stun claims similarly sell a lockdown that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Every stun claim replaced with the real behaviour (the chain pulls you in, so W lands in the same beat); Wind Wall stated at 25 seconds; Last Breath reframed as a follow-up onto his own tornado or a teammate's CC, never an opener.

audit.why: Wind Wall is correctly identified as the matchup-defining cooldown and the bait-then-commit pattern is right; it just needed the real number.
audit.corrected: 25 seconds written into the mid text.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] said Wind Wall eats 'your Q and your E2 chain'.
audit.why: Sylas's E recast carries the projectile flag and Riot's text has him throwing his chains out — Wind Wall blocks it. Chain Lash carries no projectile flag; Riot describes it as lashing out to intersect at a targeted location, which is a ground-targeted zone rather than a travelling projectile.
audit.corrected: Narrowed to the E2 chain, which is the interaction I can support from the kit.
sources: _kits/sylas.json Q (no projectile flag) vs E (projectile flag)

edits.before: E unlocks and his habit of walking up to stack Q becomes a free E2 hook target — land the chain into W stun and you win the first real trade of the lane.
edits.after: E unlocks and his habit of walking up to stack Q becomes a free E2 target — the chain pulls you onto him, so land W in the same beat and win the first trade.

edits.before: Hijack gives you Last Breath and flips the all-in math: you threaten the exact knockup-into-ult combo that defines his identity, and he cannot steal anything meaningful from you in return.
edits.after: Hijack gives you Last Breath, though it only fires onto an Airborne champion — hold it as follow-up on his own tornado or your jungler's CC, and note he has nothing to steal back from you.

edits.before: E comes online and you can hook-stun Yasuo mid-dash — his Steel Tempest habit of stepping forward to stack Q is a free E2 landing.
edits.after: E comes online and you can chain onto Yasuo mid-dash — his habit of stepping forward to stack Steel Tempest is a free E2 landing.

edits.before: Hijack grants you Last Breath — you now threaten the exact knockup-into-ult combo Yasuo needs, and he has nothing to steal back.
edits.after: Hijack grants you Last Breath — but it only lands on an Airborne target, so it is a follow-up to his tornado, never an opener.

edits.before: At level 1 you have only Q and nothing to hook him with — farm with the tips of your chain and do not chase his level-1 Steel Tempest stacking. The moment you hit level 2 and E unlocks, the dynamic flips: Yasuo loves to step forward to stack Q, and that forward step is exactly the range for your E2 hook. E1 forward to close distance, absorb whatever he throws on the E1 shield, then E2 chain him in place and land W while he is stunned. His Wind Wall cannot eat a chain that has already connected. By level 3 you have passive Petricite Burst autos to weave between spells, and your Q slow into a W heal cycle lets you sustain through any short trade he forces.
edits.after: At level 1 you have only Q and nothing to hook him with — farm with the tips of your chain and do not chase his level-1 Steel Tempest stacking. The moment you hit level 2 and E unlocks, the dynamic flips: Yasuo loves to step forward to stack Q, and that forward step is exactly the range for your E2. E1 forward to close distance, absorb whatever he throws, then E2 pulls you onto him and W lands in the same beat. Wind Wall cannot eat a chain that already connected, but it swallows one in flight — throw E2 from a side angle, never through the wall. By level 3 your passive autos weave between spells and Q slow into W heal sustains you through any short trade.

edits.before: The key discipline from levels 4-5 is Wind Wall tracking — it is a long cooldown and Yasuo always places it reactively when he sees you step up. Throw one Q to bait it, watch it go up, count to roughly 26 seconds, then commit your full E2-Q-W rotation while he has nothing to block it. At 6 you gain access to his Last Breath, which means you now threaten a knockup-into-R burst that he cannot mirror back. Every 2v2 and river skirmish from this point forward is weighted in your favour because your stolen Last Breath is a second fight-winner on top of your sustain.
edits.after: The key discipline from levels 4-5 is Wind Wall tracking — 25 seconds at rank 1, and Yasuo places it reactively the moment he sees you step up. Bait it, watch it go up, count the 25 out, then commit your full E2-Q-W rotation while he has nothing to swallow the chain. At 6 you gain his Last Breath, but read the condition: it blinks only to an Airborne champion, and nothing in your own kit knocks up. Hold it as a follow-up to his own tornado or your jungler's CC and it is a second fight-winner in every river skirmish; press it on an unairborne target and it simply will not cast.

edits.before: Use E1 dash-shield to absorb his Steel Tempest knockup or passive tornado, then immediately counter with E2 stun into W
edits.after: Dodge his two-stack Steel Tempest tornado with the E1 dash, then counter with E2 into W — the chain pulls, it never stuns

edits.before: Steal Last Breath at level 6 and use it to initiate or follow up on any knocked-up target — he cannot R back
edits.after: Steal Last Breath but hold it — it only casts onto an Airborne target and your own kit has no knockup

edits.before: Place Wind Wall to eat your Q and your E2 chain whenever you try to commit to a trade
edits.after: Place Wind Wall to swallow your E2 chain in flight the moment you commit to a trade

notes: The most serious defect here was the level 6 advice: the page told the player to steal Last Breath and use it to initiate, but Riot's text is explicit that it blinks to an Airborne enemy champion, and Sylas has no knockup anywhere in his kit. Pressed as an opener it does not cast. Also removed four separate claims that Sylas's E stuns. I left every 'E1 shield' reference alone across this page even though Riot's E text mentions no shield — needsResearch is empty by design, so absence is unknown, not a denial; flagged in unverified. The Wind-Wall-blocks-Q correction is Medium confidence, based on Chain Lash carrying no projectile flag while the E recast does.
